title: Display "Hello World"
note: Prints the text Hello World using printf. Every C program starts running from main().

title: Read and print student details
note: Reads the name, roll number and marks with scanf, then prints them with labels. The name uses %49[^\n] so it can contain spaces.

title: Perform arithmetic operations
note: Reads two integers and prints their sum, difference, product, quotient and remainder. Division is skipped when the second number is 0.

title: Convert temperature (°C ↔ °F)
note: Converts Celsius to Fahrenheit with F = C*9/5 + 32, and Fahrenheit to Celsius with C = (F-32)*5/9.

title: Calculate simple and compound interest
note: Simple interest is P*R*T/100. Compound interest is P*(1+R/100)^T - P, computed with pow() from math.h.

title: Evaluate arithmetic expressions.
note: Evaluates several expressions on three numbers to show that * / % are done before + - and that brackets change the order.

title: Demonstrate relational and logical operators.
note: Prints the result of each relational and logical operator. C shows true as 1 and false as 0.

title: Demonstrate increment/decrement operators.
note: Shows that x++ gives the old value before increasing, while ++x increases first and then gives the new value. The same holds for -- .

title: Demonstrate assignment operators.
note: Applies +=, -=, *=, /= and %= one after another to a variable and prints the value after each step.

title: Find the maximum of three numbers using the conditional operator
note: Uses the conditional operator (condition ? a : b), nested once, to pick the largest of three numbers.

title: Check whether a number is even or odd
note: If the remainder of n divided by 2 is 0 the number is even, otherwise it is odd.

title: Find the largest among three numbers
note: Compares a with b first, then compares the winner with c using nested if statements.

title: Determine whether a year is a leap year
note: A year is a leap year if divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. An if-else-if chain checks these rules in order.

title: Calculate grades based on marks
note: An if-else-if ladder checks the marks from the highest grade boundary downwards and prints the first grade that matches.

title: Develop a menu-driven calculator using switch
note: Shows a menu inside a do-while loop and uses switch to pick the operation. The loop ends when the user enters 5.

title: Generate multiplication tables
note: A for loop runs i from 1 to 10 and prints n x i for each value.

title: Compute factorial of a number
note: Multiplies 1*2*...*n in a loop using unsigned long long. Negative numbers are rejected and n above 20 would overflow.

title: Generate Fibonacci series
note: Starts with 0 and 1; each new term is the sum of the previous two. The loop prints the requested number of terms.

title: Check prime numbers
note: Tries every divisor from 2 while i*i <= n. If any divides n it is not prime; numbers below 2 are not prime.

title: Check Armstrong, palindrome, perfect, and strong numbers
note: Four small functions test the number: Armstrong (digit powers sum to n), palindrome (reverse equals n), perfect (proper divisors sum to n) and strong (digit factorials sum to n).

title: Perform arithmetic operations
note: add, subtract, multiply and divide are separate functions that main() calls with the two numbers and prints the returned values.

title: Find GCD and LCM
note: The gcd function uses Euclid's algorithm (repeat a, b = b, a%b until b is 0). The LCM is then a*b divided by the GCD.

title: Compute factorial
note: The factorial function multiplies 1 to n in a loop and returns the result to main().

title: Find power of a number
note: The power function multiplies the base by itself exp times in a loop and returns the result.

title: Demonstrate parameter passing using call by value concept.
note: swap() receives copies of x and y, so swapping them inside the function changes only the copies. The before and after values in main() are the same.

title: Factorial
note: Recursion: factorial(n) calls factorial(n-1) and multiplies by n, until it reaches 0 where it returns 1.

title: Sum of first N natural numbers
note: sum(n) returns n plus sum(n-1). The recursion stops when n is 0, which returns 0.

title: Fibonacci series
note: A loop prints fib(0) to fib(n-1). Each fib(i) is computed recursively as fib(i-1) + fib(i-2), with fib(0)=0 and fib(1)=1.

title: GCD of two numbers
note: Euclid's method: gcd(a, b) is the same as gcd(b, a % b). When b becomes 0, the answer is a.

title: Tower of Hanoi
note: To move n disks, first move n-1 disks to the spare peg, then move the biggest disk, then move the n-1 disks on top of it. Each step is printed.

title: Find sum and average of array elements
note: Reads the elements into an array while adding them up. The average is the sum divided by the number of elements.

title: Find largest and smallest element in an array
note: Starts by assuming the first element is both largest and smallest, then compares every other element and updates them.

title: Reverse an array
note: Swaps the first element with the last, the second with the second-last, and so on until the middle is reached.

title: Merge two arrays
note: Copies all elements of the first array into a new array, then copies the elements of the second array right after them.

title: Remove duplicate elements in an array
note: Builds a new array of unique values: an element is added only if it is not already present in the new array.

title: Find string length without strlen()
note: Reads the line with fgets, removes the newline, then counts characters one by one until the end-of-string character '\0'.

title: Copy and concatenate strings
note: Copies and joins the strings character by character with loops, and then repeats the same tasks using strcpy() and strcat() so the results can be compared.

title: Compare two strings
note: Moves along both strings while the characters match. If both strings end together they are equal. The result is also checked with strcmp().

title: Reverse a string
note: Finds the length, then swaps the first and last characters, the second and second-last, and so on.

title: Check palindrome and count vowels, digits, and special characters
note: Compares characters from both ends to check for a palindrome, then goes through the string once, counting vowels, digits and special characters (anything that is not a letter, digit or space).

title: Matrix addition
note: Both matrices must have the same size. Each element of the result is the sum of the elements at the same position.

title: Matrix subtraction
note: Both matrices must have the same size. Each element of the result is the first matrix element minus the second matrix element at the same position.

title: Matrix multiplication
note: The columns of the first matrix must equal the rows of the second. Each result element is the sum of products of a row of the first matrix with a column of the second.

title: Matrix transpose
note: The transpose swaps rows and columns, so element [i][j] of the original becomes element [j][i].

title: Check whether a matrix is symmetric
note: A symmetric matrix must be square and equal to its transpose. The program compares each element with its mirror across the diagonal.

title: Demonstrate pointer arithmetic.
note: Adding 1 to an int pointer moves it to the next int, not the next byte. Subtracting two pointers gives the number of elements between them.

title: Access one-dimensional arrays using pointers.
note: The name of an array is the address of its first element, so *(p + i) is the same as arr[i]. The program reads and prints the array using pointer notation.

title: Swap two numbers using call by reference.
note: The addresses of x and y are passed to swap(), which uses * to exchange the values stored there. This is why the change is visible in main().

title: Find the largest element in an array using pointers.
note: A pointer walks through the array, and the largest value seen so far is kept in max. The pointer is dereferenced with * to compare each element.

title: Demonstrate arrays of pointers.
note: An array of int pointers holds the addresses of three variables, and an array of char pointers holds four strings. Changing *nums[1] changes the original variable b.

title: malloc()
note: malloc reserves memory on the heap for n integers at run time, and returns NULL if it fails. The memory is used like an array and released with free().

title: calloc()
note: calloc reserves memory like malloc but sets every element to zero, which the first output line shows. The array is then filled with new values.

title: realloc()
note: realloc makes the array bigger while keeping the old values. A temporary pointer is used so the original array is not lost if realloc fails.

title: free()
note: free() returns heap memory to the system. After freeing, the pointer is set to NULL to avoid using a dangling pointer, and forgetting free() would cause a memory leak.

title: Dynamically allocate memory for a matrix
note: An array of row pointers (int **) is allocated first, then each row gets its own array of columns. To free it, every row is freed first and then the array of pointers.

title: Demonstrate structures, unions and typedef.
note: A struct stores all its members separately, while a union's members share the same memory, so its size is that of the largest member. typedef gives the types shorter names.

title: Pass structures to functions and manipulate structures using pointers.
note: display() receives a copy of the structure, so it cannot change the original. add_bonus() receives a pointer and uses -> to update the marks in the original.

title: Create and write to a text file
note: fopen with mode "w" creates students.txt, and fprintf writes one student record per line. The file is closed with fclose when done.

title: Read and display file contents
note: fopen with mode "r" opens students.txt, and fgets reads it one line at a time until the end. If the file does not exist, a clear error message is shown.

title: Append records to a file
note: Mode "a" adds new records at the end of students.txt without erasing the old ones. The file is then reopened for reading to display all records.

title: Demonstrate bitwise operators (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, shift)
note: Each operator works on the bits of the numbers, and the results are shown in decimal and 8-bit binary. A small function prints the bits using shift and AND.

title: Demonstrate bit fields in a structure
note: Bit fields let a structure member use only a fixed number of bits, so a date fits in 16 bits. The size is compared with an ordinary structure holding the same data.

title: Demonstrate enumerations (e.g., days of week, traffic light states)
note: An enum gives names to integer constants, starting from 0. A switch statement uses these names to decide whether it is a weekend and what a traffic light means.

title: Demonstrate command line arguments (sum of numbers passed as arguments)
note: The values typed after the program name are stored as strings in argv. The program converts each one to an integer with atoi and adds them up, and prints a usage message if none are given.

title: Demonstrate macros and preprocessor directives (#define, #ifdef, conditional compilation)
note: #define creates constants and function-like macros, which the preprocessor replaces before compilation. #ifdef, #ifndef and #if include or skip code depending on conditions, and __LINE__ gives the current line number.
